Sound Familiar?

If you're here, you've probably already tried the obvious fixes.

Case Type — Reactivity

Barking and lunging on the lead

Walks have become something to dread rather than enjoy — crossing the road to avoid other dogs, bracing for the next reaction.

Case Type — Guarding

Resource guarding

Growling or snapping over food, toys, beds or spaces — behaviour that makes home feel unpredictable.

Case Type — Aggression

Aggression toward people or dogs

Incidents that leave you anxious about visitors, walks, or other dogs approaching — and unsure what happens next.

Case Type — Separation

Separation-related distress

Barking, destruction or panic the moment you leave — making normal life logistically difficult.

Case Type — Recall

No reliable recall

Off-lead freedom feels like a gamble rather than something you can trust, so it rarely happens.

Case Type — Anxiety

Fear that limits daily life

A dog who shuts down or panics around triggers most dogs take in their stride — vets, visitors, noise, new places.

None of this makes your dog "bad," and it doesn't make you a bad owner. These are communication problems, built up over time — and they're solvable with the right process.

Methodology

Training the whole picture, not just the behaviour.

Obedience commands can look impressive without changing anything underneath. We work differently — treating the behaviour as information, not the enemy.

Practical, not theoretical

Training happens in the real environments your dog actually struggles in — the park, the doorway, the dinner table — not just a quiet room with no distractions.

Balanced, case-by-case methods

We do use equipment — including e-collars — as part of our training. What matters is how: every tool is introduced fairly, clearly, and only when a dog's specific case calls for it, so your dog always understands what's being asked. No ideology, no shortcuts, no guesswork.

Root cause, not symptom control

Every case starts with understanding why the behaviour exists — fear, frustration, or a learned pattern — so the change holds long after we've left.

Owner-led, for the long term

Unlike a board-and-train, we don't take your dog away and hand them back "fixed." We teach you to manage, handle and work through your dog's behaviour yourself — because without that knowledge, the behaviour tends to come straight back. You leave with the skills, not a temporary result.

Programme — Session-Based Training

A focused path from chaos to calm — for as long as it takes.

We don't work to a fixed number of weeks or sessions. We keep working with you, session by session, until your dog's behaviour is genuinely resolved — and every session is run with you handling your own dog, so you leave with real, hands-on experience, not just a demonstration.

S1
Motivation, equipment & recall foundations
We start by building your dog's motivation to work with you, fitting and introducing any equipment properly, and laying the first foundations of a reliable recall.
S2
Structure, triggers & recall building
We introduce fair, clear correction alongside the groundwork already in place, then start working around your dog's specific triggers while continuing to build recall.
S3
Into the real world
Training moves out into open, real-life areas around your dog's triggers, with a focus on loose-leash walking and settle work in public.
S4+
Real-life scenarios & fine-tuning
We go further into real-life scenarios — closer trigger work in increasingly challenging environments — and tidy up any remaining issues as they come up. We continue at this stage for as many sessions as your dog needs.

This shows the shape of how we work, not a fixed plan. Every case is different — some dogs need four sessions, others need many more. We keep going until the behaviour is properly resolved, not until a package runs out.

Meet the Team

A husband-and-wife team, grounded in real homes.

Durham Dog Academy is run by us — a husband-and-wife team, together with the two dogs who inspired our logo. We work with all kinds of dogs, not just the toughest cases: as much about helping a dog become calmer and more well-rounded, and rebuilding the relationship between dog and owner, as it is about resolving serious reactivity or aggression.

Our training certification comes from the Yorkshire Canine Academy's dog trainer development programme, and our approach is a balanced one: every dog and every case is assessed on its own terms, with methods chosen to fit — not a fixed script. We work with you at your own home and out in the real-world places your dog needs to learn in, across Durham and the wider North East.

Balanced trainer Yorkshire Canine Academy cert. Fully insured In-home & out in the community

FAQ

Common questions before applying.

Obedience classes teach commands in a controlled setting. We work on the underlying behaviour itself — why your dog reacts the way it does — and apply that in the real environments where it actually happens, so the change transfers to everyday life.
Yes — this is a core part of our work. Every application involving aggression is reviewed carefully before acceptance, and we'll ask detailed questions about the history so we can judge fit and safety before we begin.
We're a balanced trainer. Every case starts with reward-based, force-free foundations — that's true for every dog we work with. Where a case genuinely needs it, we'll introduce additional tools, including e-collars, used fairly, precisely, and only to the degree that dog and situation require. Nothing is one-size-fits-all, and we'll always explain exactly what we're using and why before we use it.
There's no fixed length — we work in sessions, not weeks, and we keep going until your dog's behaviour is genuinely resolved. Some dogs need four or five sessions, others need more, depending on the case. You handle your own dog in every session, so you're building real experience throughout.
A mix of both. Training typically includes in-home sessions and work out in the real-world locations relevant to your dog's case, across Durham and the wider North East.
We review every application personally. If it looks like a good fit, we'll follow up with a few extra questions and book a short discovery call to talk through your dog's case before confirming a place.
